title: Secret audit misses credentials in Write tool contents
expected: The masked audit finds credentials stored in a recorded Write.content value.
observed: The synthetic Write call contains a password assignment. secrets --json exits 1 with no finding. secrets clean previews one replacement in the same file.
impact: A rotation worklist can incorrectly report a clean session containing a stored credential. The same omission can affect other tool input fields hidden by the display summary.
acceptance: Scan relevant decoded record values rather than only display summaries
Keep credential values out of text and JSON output
Add a test asserting that audit and clean agree on this Write fixture

title: Time filters compare timestamp strings instead of instants
expected: Session membership follows the UTC half-open interval [since, before), independent of timestamp precision and offset spelling.
observed: A session at 12:00:00.123Z is excluded by --before 12:00:00.123001Z. A session at 13:00:00+02:00 is excluded by --before 12:00:00Z even though it started at 11:00 UTC.
impact: Searches can omit the requested historical sessions or include sessions outside a time boundary.
acceptance: Normalize both stored timestamps and bounds before comparing
Check inclusive since and exclusive before for equivalent offsets and mixed fractional precision
Preserve @N and today semantics

title: Counted Claude API errors disappear from the errors view
expected: A Claude isApiErrorMessage record counted as an error can be inspected with errors and show --errors.
observed: list --json reports errors=1 for the fixture, while errors --json returns no records and exits 1.
impact: The aggregate error count points to a failure that the dedicated error view cannot retrieve.
acceptance: Carry isApiErrorMessage into canonical error annotations
Return the original failed record in errors and show --errors
Keep list and stats error counts consistent
requirement_basis: Consistency between counted record properties and the errors command

title: Normalized find matches can produce excerpts with no matching text
expected: The excerpt for a normalized match shows the original source occurrence, including diacritic-insensitive matches.
observed: Query cafe matches a long event ending in café, but the returned excerpt contains only its leading padding. The match lies beyond the excerpt because position lookup uses unnormalized substring search.
impact: Agents receive a correctly matched session with evidence that does not demonstrate why it matched.
acceptance: Locate excerpt spans using tokenization compatible with ranked matching
Retain a mapping to original source character positions
Test long events with diacritics and normalization differences

title: show, prompts and errors ignore row limits in JSON mode
expected: -n 1 returns at most one JSONL record, keeping that record complete.
observed: The fixtures return 7 records from show, 3 from prompts, and 2 from errors with --json -n 1. cmds honors the same combination.
impact: Consumers cannot bound these read responses and may load an entire large transcript unexpectedly.
acceptance: Apply row selection limits before JSON serialization
Keep returned records unmodified
Report omissions through stderr or a documented metadata channel
Verify -n 0 still returns all records

title: errors applies text limits per session and hides omissions
expected: The errors -n limit applies to the entire selected scope and a shortened view states the omitted count.
observed: errors @1:@2 -n 1 prints two error rows. A single session with two errors prints one row but only reports a total of two errors, without stating one row was omitted.
impact: Range scans exceed the requested budget and users can mistake a shortened list for the complete set of failures.
acceptance: Track a scope-wide emitted-row count
Show a precise omitted-record notice
Cover multi-session and single-session limits

title: tools, stats, path and clean accept but ignore -n
expected: Commands that advertise a printed-row limit honor it, or reject an unsupported option.
observed: With -n 1, tools prints two tool rows, stats prints 17 field rows, and path prints both parent and child paths. A clean preview also prints both selected file rows with -n 1.
impact: The shared option appears valid while providing no control over these outputs.
acceptance: Implement consistent row limits with omission notices or remove unsupported command options
Preserve explicit-file scope and unlimited zero semantics

title: --full still trims long transcript text
expected: --full prints whole text, as both the help epilog and agent primer state.
observed: show --full trims a synthetic user message larger than the default 40,000-character scan budget. --around correctly preserves the full text.
impact: An agent following the documented recovery flag still loses content.
acceptance: Treat --full as disabling text trimming, or consistently change the published contract
Add a long-record CLI check distinct from ordinary full-kind selection

title: Skill input counts multiply when calls share a record
expected: Two Skill blocks calling notify and review produce one input count for each.
observed: calls reports Skill=2, but skill_inputs reports notify=2 and review=2. Each Skill event rescans all tool_use blocks in the original physical record.
impact: Per-skill usage reports overcount batched tool calls.
acceptance: Associate each event with its own input block or count each physical block once
Test two Skill calls plus an unrelated tool in the same record

title: Empty show selections exit successfully only in text mode
expected: An empty selection returns exit 1 regardless of output format.
observed: show --type does-not-exist exits 0, while the same command with --json exits 1.
impact: Scripts that use the documented exit code treat missing evidence as a successful result.
acceptance: Return the same empty-result status for text and JSON
Check empty type, range and around selections

title: --tail 0 returns the entire selected transcript
expected: Last zero events produces an empty selection; only -n 0 is documented as unlimited.
observed: Python's [-0:] slice returns the complete selection, so --tail 0 --json emits every skeleton record.
impact: A computed zero tail count can unexpectedly print a large transcript.
acceptance: Handle zero explicitly or reject it with documented usage guidance
Validate negative tail counts
Keep positive tail order unchanged
requirement_basis: Inferred boundary behavior from 'Last N selected events' and the separate -n 0 convention

title: Negative row limits are accepted inconsistently
expected: A negative row count is a usage error, as already enforced by find and skills.
observed: list, show, prompts, errors, tools, stats and cmds all accept -n -1 and exit 0. Some slice off a row, some emit none and some ignore the value.
impact: A malformed calculated limit silently changes output instead of reporting the mistake.
acceptance: Validate shared limits centrally as integers >= 0
Apply validation at every supported flag position
Retain the documented zero meaning
requirement_basis: Inferred consistency requirement with existing find/skills validation

title: path and secrets clean accept --json but emit plain text
expected: An accepted --json option emits structured output, or the command rejects the unsupported option.
observed: The clean command advertises --json, accepts it and exits 0, but stdout contains a TSV header, data row and dry-run prose. path --json likewise accepts the option and returns a plain pathname.
impact: Automation piping a clean preview to a JSON reader fails despite using an accepted flag.
acceptance: Implement JSON output for preview/apply results or reject the flag clearly
Keep diagnostics separate and credential values masked

title: Limited secret worklists understate the number of findings
expected: A worklist limited with -n reports the full distinct count and number omitted.
observed: Two different synthetic password values are detected. With -n 1, the footer says '1 distinct secrets' and provides no omitted-count notice.
impact: A user can stop rotating credentials after the one displayed row because the summary hides the remaining finding.
acceptance: Compute totals before slicing
Report shown, total and omitted counts
Keep returned fingerprints stable across limited and unlimited views

title: A non-object JSONL record crashes transcript reads
expected: A structurally invalid record is skipped or reported through a controlled error without losing source-coordinate integrity.
observed: A valid user record followed by JSON number 42 makes show --full exit 1 with an AttributeError traceback rather than a diagnostic.
impact: One malformed record can make otherwise readable session evidence inaccessible and is reported using the documented empty-result exit code.
acceptance: Validate decoded record shapes before accessing mapping fields
Keep later valid records readable or clearly mark the read incomplete
Apply the same policy to both providers and cache parsing
requirement_basis: Resilience expectation based on supported malformed/torn JSONL handling

title: Primer filesystem failures escape as Python tracebacks
expected: An invalid or unwritable destination returns a useful filesystem diagnostic with exit 2.
observed: init --write not-a-directory/AGENTS.md, where not-a-directory is an existing regular file, exits 1 with a FileExistsError traceback.
impact: Setup automation receives the empty/stale status for a real write error, with an unnecessarily long exception dump.
acceptance: Catch relevant filesystem errors at the command boundary
Report the destination and error on stderr
Keep the original file intact

title: The documented empty-result exit code omits the list exception
expected: The exit-code reference clearly describes list returning 0 for an empty scope, if that deliberate exception remains.
observed: README and top-level help say exit 1 means an empty result. list_scope explicitly returns 0 for an empty scope, and test_empty_json_list_keeps_stdout_machine_readable asserts that behavior.
impact: Consumers following the global exit-code description cannot infer whether an empty listing is a miss or a successful command.
acceptance: Document the empty-list exception in the README and help, or adopt a consistent behavior after reviewing compatibility
Keep the primer exit-code guidance consistent with the chosen rule
requirement_basis: Documentation consistency, confirmed by the existing empty-list CLI test
